status: SEED — THRESHOLDS UNCHANGED FROM v0.1 AND STILL GUESSES. v0.2 repairs the lexicons only: word-boundary matching, explicit stems marked with a trailing *, and removal of terms that matched ordinary catalog prose. Requires the build_matchers patch in SCORE_PATCH_v0.2.md — without it the * stems are matched literally and every stem goes dead.
measures: What a school's catalog offers. Not what a graduate leaves with, and not what is required — see limitations.
limitations: OFFERED, NOT REQUIRED. harvest.py reads course descriptions, not degree requirement sheets, so nothing here can distinguish a required professional-practice course from an elective nobody takes. The Venture axis in particular means much less without it. Either harvest program pages, or state plainly that edition one measures offering.

Denominator is the whole catalog, not the art catalog. A large public university dilutes: 40 art-business courses among 6,000 total scores lower than 10 among 400. Normalizing by CIP-50-relevant courses rather than all courses is unresolved.
Thresholds below are placeholders. They must be set from the observed distribution once enough schools are scored, and the rule used must be published.

technology.name: Art Technology Adoption
technology.question: Does this course teach making with computational or emerging tools, as practice rather than as a topic to discuss?
includes: generative and AI tools used in making
creative coding, computational design, procedural work
digital fabrication, CNC, 3D printing
immersive, XR, virtual production, game engines
emerging media and hybrid analog-digital practice
excludes: general computer literacy or office software
art history or theory courses that discuss technology without making
IT, computer science, or engineering courses outside the arts

venture.name: Entrepreneurship and Art Venture Training
venture.question: Does this course teach the business of an independent creative practice — money, contracts, clients, running a studio?
includes: professional practice, business of art, career preparation for artists
pricing, valuation, negotiation
contracts, copyright, licensing, intellectual property for creators
grant writing, fundraising, patronage
studio operations, freelancing, self-employment, taxes
entrepreneurship and venture formation in a creative context
excludes: general business school courses with no creative-practice framing
arts administration or nonprofit management training administrators rather than artists
internship placeholders with no instructional content

self.name: Creative Self-Development Science
self.question: Does this course teach creative process itself — how ideas form, how practice sustains — as distinct from technique or history?
includes: creativity science, creative cognition, problem finding
flow, deliberate practice, habit and process
ideation and idea development taught as method
contemplative, somatic, or embodiment practice
critique method taught explicitly as a practice
artist wellbeing, burnout, long-arc practice sustainability
excludes: any studio course that merely involves making
psychology courses outside the arts unit
art therapy training clinicians rather than artists

audience.name: Audience and Distribution
audience.question: Does this course teach reaching and holding an audience without a gatekeeper?
includes: exhibition and curatorial practice
documentation of one's own work
writing or speaking about one's own work, artist statements
publishing, self-publishing, distribution
digital platform and audience development, social media as practice
socially engaged, community-based, and public art
excludes: communications or PR courses outside the arts unit
museum studies training curators rather than artists

prefilter.note: Stage one is tuned for RECALL, not precision. Over-matching is fine and expected; stage two removes the false positives. Under-matching is invisible and unrecoverable, so err wide.

classifier.note: Temperature 0 and a cached result per course-text hash, so a rerun reproduces exactly. Every classification is logged with the model and rubric version.

matching.rule: Each term is compiled with word boundaries. A trailing * means prefix match: 'negotiat*' matches negotiate, negotiating, negotiation.
matching.why: v0.1 stripped whitespace off every term before escaping it, so ' ai ' compiled to a bare substring 'ai' and matched painting, detail, available, maintain, chair. 'unity' matched community. 'tax' matched taxonomy. 'contract' matched contraction. On an art catalog the technology axis matched close to everything, which makes the shortlist rate useless as a diagnostic.

flagged_for_author.note: Not changed in v0.2 — each is an editorial call, not a mechanical repair. Run lexprobe.py and decide from the counts and samples.

probably_dead_phrases.why: No registrar writes these. A dead term cannot lower a score, only fail to raise one — so the Self axis scoring near zero would be manufactured by the lexicon rather than found in the world. That is the index's strongest sentence and it must not be an artifact.

high_carry_boilerplate.why: Catalog boilerplate ('prepares students for careers in...', 'satisfies the general education distribution requirement', 'unity of composition'). Stage two rejects them correctly, but if one term carries >40% of an axis's shortlist the axis is measuring that word. Check carry% in lexprobe before spending on stage two.
